Quality-of-life wave, inspired by a feature comparison against Zipline — adopting what fits featherdrop's zero-knowledge, no-accounts philosophy and hardening the rest. Just update the container; `/data` and `/config` are untouched.

### Added
1. **Paste to upload.** Ctrl/Cmd+V anywhere on the page drops the clipboard's files (e.g. a screenshot) straight into the selection — pasting into text fields is untouched.
2. **Remembered options.** Your last-used expiry, download limit and metadata choice are restored on the next visit (locally, never the password). The operator's `DEFAULT_EXPIRY` is honoured again as the starting value — the SPA had been ignoring it.
3. **Photo metadata removal.** JPEGs can be scrubbed of EXIF/GPS/IPTC **in the browser, before encryption** (the server never sees plaintext — this is the only place it can happen). On by default when a JPEG is selected, one switch to keep the metadata; a photo that can't be parsed is uploaded untouched rather than risked.
4. **Install it as an app (PWA).** featherdrop is installable and registers as an **Android share target**: "Share → featherdrop" from any app drops the shared files into the normal upload flow.
5. **Operator guardrails.** New envs, all optional: `MAX_EXPIRY` (cap the longest expiry — the UI hides longer options and the server rejects them), `STORAGE_QUOTA` (total-bytes cap, rejects over-quota uploads with HTTP 507 before any byte lands), `RATE_LIMIT` (per-IP token buckets on upload/finalize/download+password attempts, on by default, 429 + `Retry-After`), `TRUST_PROXY` (key limits on `X-Forwarded-For` behind a reverse proxy). Together they make an internet-reachable instance a reasonable thing to run.
6. **Container healthcheck.** `GET /api/healthcheck` plus a Dockerfile `HEALTHCHECK` (self-check flag — works in the distroless image), so Docker/Unraid show a real health state.

### Changed
7. **Share pages opt out of search engines**: `robots.txt` plus `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow` on all share/download responses (uniform across 200/401/404 — no existence side-channel).
8. **Boot-time config validation**: invalid values for the new envs abort with a clear message naming the variable; a non-absolute `BASE_URL` and a short `UPLOAD_PASSWORD` log warnings.

### Security notes
9. An audit of the delete/finalize/download paths (prompted by the recent CVE round in a comparable project) found no gaps: all token comparisons are constant-time, 404s are uniform, and no unauthenticated mutation route exists. The new rate limiter now also throttles the key-verifier guessing surface.
